t: Nour Abbas of Deir Hanna went from bus driver to heavy-truck driver
d: The 32-year-old mother of two is one of very few Arab women in the trade.

t: Count reaches 186 after an 81-year-old is shot dead in Shefa-Amr
d: The Abraham Initiatives' tally of Arab citizens and residents killed this year rose to 186 after Ibrahim Bashkar died of gunshot wounds.

t: Final polls give the two Arab lists between 14 and 16 seats
d: All three TV polls put the Joint List at 9; Ra'am ranges from 5 to 7, and neither bloc reaches 61.

t: Sakhnin school tops national table for excellence matriculation, 82.4%
d: 103 of 125 graduates of al-Bashaer school earned the distinguished certificate, ministry data show.

t: Police say murders in Arab society fell about 14% this year
d: Commissioner Danny Levy called the figures the best in three years, but the statement gave no underlying numbers.

t: Smotrich's party says 800 families signed up for new Negev and Galilee towns
d: Religious Zionism says the plan for 40 new towns aims to add a million Jews and to cancel approved plans in Arab towns.

t: Authorities demolish a wedding hall in Deir Hanna days before the vote
d: Police sealed off the area while bulldozers took down the hall, said to be built without a permit.

t: Supreme Court bars party observers from sending live voter counts
d: Polling-station members may not digitally tally who has voted and pass it to parties in real time.

t: Life sentence for man who set Rafe Harsha alight in his bed in Maisar
d: The Haifa court also ordered the maximum NIS 258,000 compensation to the victim's son.

t: Pollsters expect Arab turnout near 63%, well up on 2022
d: Stat-Net forecasts 63%; Maariv's poll found intent to vote among Arab-party supporters up to 81%.

t: Second family in days demolishes its own home in Umm al-Fahm
d: Saeed Ighbariya tore down his house in al-Ayoun before bulldozers arrived, to avoid the state's bill.

t: Two relatives arrested over the June killing of Asma Abu Ghanem, 19, in Ramla
d: The arrests come about four months after she was killed in the Jawarish neighbourhood.

t: Four Arab women students doused with drinks and called 'terrorists' in Jerusalem
d: The students, from Tayibe, Qalansawe and Baqa al-Gharbiya, say the attack was filmed for social media.

t: Anonymous campaign against Ra'am traced to firms tied to Channel 14's owner
d: FakeReporter says billboards and Arabic polling link to companies of Yitzhak Mirilashvili.

t: Interior Ministry keeps al-Qaisoum council head, replaces members with appointed panel
d: The council failed to pass its 2026 budget; the ministry blamed the opposing members rather than chairman Jabr Abu Kaf.

t: Students stop Ben Gvir from speaking at Tel Aviv University
d: Dozens from the Standing Together campus cell stood on chairs and chanted until he could not deliver his speech.

t: At Haifa rally, protesters call for Arab and Jewish turnout on 27 October
d: The anti-government demonstration at Horev Centre featured Ehud Olmert and bereaved families.

t: Arab citizens still under 2% of hi-tech workers, Hasoub chairman says
d: Ayman Saif told the group's annual conference the path to the industry is still long.

t: Twenty-year-old demolition orders in Tayibe scheduled for election day
d: Attorney Qais Nasser says the State Comptroller's office is examining the timing.

t: Democrats pledge NIS 1 billion a year against crime and a demolitions freeze
d: At a Nazareth event the party said it would seek the internal security portfolio.

t: Arabic speakers are 23% of first graders; Shoresh warns on education gaps
d: Arabic-speaking pupils scored below every OECD country in PISA 2025, the institute's report says.

t: ACRI asks government not to divert NIS 964 million from future Arab plan
d: Finance Minister Smotrich proposed using money set aside for a coming plan for Arab society to bring forward defence purchases.

t: Tel Aviv University to award honorary doctorate to Umm al-Fahm museum founder
d: Artist Said Abu Shakra founded the Umm al-Fahm Art Gallery thirty years ago with his brother Farid.

t: Two young men shot dead in Segev Shalom and Umm al-Fahm within a day
d: Yassin al-Shawi was killed in a suspected family feud in the Negev; Nimer Jabareen, 20, was shot in Umm al-Fahm the next morning.

t: War cut Arab employment harder than Jewish, Alfanar director says
d: Arab men's employment fell about 27% at the start of the war, against 11% for Jewish men.

t: Herzog calls crime in Arab society a disaster and wants a bigger police force
d: The president said more than 1.3 million citizens live 'under terror' and police are beyond their capacity.

t: Man arrested in Afula after punching Arab bus driver and threatening to kill him
d: The driver on line 247 said the suspect spat at him and shouted that Arabs should be killed.

t: Dozens of homes and a mosque demolished in Negev village of al-Dahiya
d: Accounts range from about 50 homes and 250 people to 80 structures and 400 people, all of the Abu Wadi family.

t: Four women arrested in Ar'ara an-Naqab; Ben Gvir says women are now arrested too
d: Police say the women threw stones at relatives in a family feud; the minister posted that his policy had changed.

t: 570 Arab citizens were hospitalised or died from gunshot wounds in 2025
d: A Haaretz report compares the figure with 67 Jewish citizens and finds most Arab violence casualties were shot.

t: Tel Aviv man, 22, charged with planned killing of Mohammed Qatwan
d: Prosecutors say Mohammed Zeitounia lured Qatwan to a meeting on 30 August, shot him and fired at two companions.

t: Mansour Abbas asks attorney general to freeze home demolitions until after the vote
d: The Ra'am leader says Ben Gvir is using demolitions in his campaign.

t: Intercity buses and trains free from the evening before election day
d: The Central Elections Committee set free travel from 8 pm on 26 October until services end on 27 October.

t: Rahat man shot and run over; police look at a parking dispute
d: Mousa Yousef al-Jabour, 26, was killed in Rahat's Neighbourhood 25, ending two weeks without a counted killing.

t: Arab bus drivers report 45 attacks this year as Umm al-Fahm driver is beaten
d: Abed Mahajna was hit in the face and racially abused after someone threw an object at his bus in Hadera.

t: Bus carrying Bnei Sakhnin fans stoned on the way home from Bloomfield
d: League chief Erez Halfon called it another red line crossed; the club asked police for protection at away games.

t: Nazareth announces 'City Palace Music Days' festival for November
d: Six evenings of Arab classical, tarab, orchestral and contemporary music at the Nazareth cultural palace.

t: Police exchange fire with armed Nazareth group in Kafr Manda, arrest four
d: Police say the group was behind shootings at businesses across the north; one suspect was wounded.

t: Shin Bet says 72 Negev residents detained on security suspicion this year
d: The agency says about 50 were indicted and describes a Segev Shalom cell it says planned an armed battalion.

t: Netanyahu promises an 'iron fist' and NIS 1 billion for a Shin Bet role
d: The prime minister posted in Arabic as funding to involve the security service in fighting Arab crime was announced.

t: Father, brother and cousin sentenced for the 2023 killing of Aya Abu Hajjaj
d: She was stabbed in Lod in front of her two small children while heavily pregnant.

t: Netanyahu asks Shin Bet for a Negev weapons plan after chief's warning
d: Shin Bet head David Zini told ministers of armed groups in Bedouin communities; an MK wants the army involved.

t: 134 Arab citizens killed on the roads this year, up 19%
d: Or Yarok counts 39% of all road deaths among Arab citizens, about twice their share of the population.

t: Bar-Ilan maths professor charged with plotting mass attacks on Arab citizens
d: Prosecutors say Shahar Nevo planned simultaneous attacks to kill hundreds and drive Arabs out of the country.

t: Protest outside Ben Gvir's home over mosque raids and call-to-prayer fines
d: Kulanu Makom co-chairs Rula Daoud and Alon-Lee Green asked whether the Arab vote frightens the minister.

t: Kafr Qara emergency conference answers incitement against Arab doctors
d: Doctors, mayors and health groups met under the slogan 'We won't let incitement harm the health system'.

t: Arab towns mark 26 years since October 2000 with a march in Arraba
d: The High Follow-Up Committee led visits to the graves of those killed and a central march.

t: About 420,000 votes were lost below the threshold in 2022, Taub Center says
d: A list may need 171,000 to 195,000 votes to enter the Knesset this time, depending on turnout.

t: Supreme Court lets Ra'am and the Joint List run; Abu Shehadeh withdraws
d: The court unanimously overturned the elections committee's bans on both lists and cleared MK Ofer Cassif by 7-2.

t: Netanya court freezes demolition of Abu Mtair family homes in Tayibe
d: The orders were more than twenty years old; five large families live in the houses.

t: Channel 13 poll: Netanyahu bloc 54, opposition 52, Arab lists 14
d: The Joint List polled 9 and Ra'am 5 at the start of the final month.

t: Ra'am adopts the unrecognised villages' plan for Negev regional councils
d: Mansour Abbas and Walid al-Huashla say recognising the villages needs a partnership in government.

t: Road deaths pass 330 but road safety is missing from most party platforms
d: State Comptroller data show 40% of Arab schools had no road-safety coordinator.

t: Eisenkot says Ra'am will not sit in a government he leads
d: He set conditions including recognising Israel as a Jewish state; Segalovitz replied there is no Eisenkot government without Ra'am.

t: Police enter Tel Sheva mosque in their shoes over a noise complaint
d: Officers and National Guard members walked onto the prayer carpets of al-Salam mosque and later fined it over the call to prayer.
